structured.approach: The step ran in check mode. I loaded the design-steps skill for DES-01. I read the two contracted inputs: the TRD and the feature override of org.architecture. I also read the org-level base files org/org.architecture.md and org/org.decision_log.md. Then I compared every platform aspect in org.architecture with what the TRD changes: repositories, runtimes, the flow between repositories, the signature rule, the JSON rules, data, tenancy and security, the LLM provider and the platform decisions. I wrote one check record with the conclusion, the evidence, observations for the Architect and the triggers that would require a full update. No connectors were needed because the inputs held all the facts; shell access is denied for this step. A verifier subagent checked the draft against the sources. I then fixed the five statements it flagged as overstated or uncited: the TRD's status, security scope, the flow between repositories, the bucket_for issue and the DES-02 references.

claims.text: The step's condition was not met in this run: the TRD does not flag a platform-level change, so DES-01 ran as a check.

The platform architecture has four repositories in one flow. ap_pipeline, ap_forecast and ap_aging run on Python 3.9; ap_portal runs on Node.js 22 CommonJS. JSON carries amounts as two-decimal strings and dates as ISO strings. The rule is 'Keep every existing signature; add new functions.'

The TRD changes only the four existing repositories (C-1 to C-10). It adds new functions (delays_by_vendor, vendor_risk, overdue_with_risk, overdue_rows_to_json, renderOverdueRisk) and makes two additive changes (to_model behaviour; risk=None as the last parameter of build_explanation_request). Its validation check records 'Pass' for the signature rule.
CT-1 sends amount as a two-decimal string and has no date field, so it follows the existing JSON rule of the platform.

The TRD adds no storage, schema migration or new persistent data. It adds one record key, paid_date. It adds or changes no finance posting, authentication, tenancy or payment execution (tier T2). The LLM provider and model do not change.

The org-level base architecture describes ap_aging as a pure Python 3.9 library 'used by the AP API', with no database, no network and no secrets, and it says existing signatures and return shapes must not change.
The TRD records new code as consistent with decisions D-2026-031, D-2026-044 and D-2026-050. It raises the existing formatAmount conflict with D-2026-044 as TQ-2.
Transport between ap_aging and ap_portal is still open (TQ-3). If its answer adds or changes a service or API, DES-01 must run as a full update.
Conclusion: no platform architecture update is needed now. The check record lists six triggers (TR-1 to TR-6) that would require one.

open_questions: PU-Q1 (non-blocking): Should the function lists in org.architecture be updated after release with the new exported functions and the risk parameter? This is housekeeping, not an architectural change.
PU-Q2 (non-blocking): Is the 'AP API' named in the org-level base org.architecture.md the transport for CT-1 (TQ-3)? If it is, trigger TR-1 applies and DES-01 should run as a full update.
PU-Q3 (non-blocking): Which document is the platform architecture of record: the four-repository feature override or the ap_aging-only org-level base document?

It adds no storage, tenancy, authentication or provider change. The record lists six triggers for a full update, the main one being the answer to TQ-3 (transport between ap_aging and ap_portal), and three non-blocking questions.
